helper_moved.name: eval_many
helper_moved.signature: fn eval_many(data: &[Fp], slices: &[(usize, usize)], point: &[Fp2]) -> Vec<Fp2>
helper_moved.from: hashline/src/layer.rs lines 210-220 at 0b2b830 (private to the module)
helper_moved.hashline_adapter: hashline/src/layer.rs imports it under the same name (`use zkp_core::ffn_v3::eval_many;`), so every call site is unchanged and hashline's public API is unchanged

purity.note: the GPU arm stays in hashline's eval_many_dev, which calls this function as its host path

why_this_one: MIGRATION.md names it in 2c blocker (i), and it is the only member of that list that is a pure function of its arguments

byte-neutral by construction: verbatim body, its only dependency (mle::eq_table_msb) was already in the core, and Fp2 addition is associative and commutative so the rayon reduction order cannot change a value
used by BOTH the v2 and the v3 prover, so cpu-v2 and cpu-v3 are live byte gates on it; hashline/src/zk.rs keeps its own private copy (zk.rs:934), so cpu-zk and cpu-zkv3 are an untouched control
ten lines of body: reviewable in one sitting

rejected.why_not: pure, but it is the LogUp helper-column BUILDER: it produces a committed column, pulls in batch_inverse2, and the ledger groups it with HostTabsV3 and the zero-check table construction, whose move is entangled with the try_helpers_commit hook and the compact-arm ruling
pure and tiny, but #[inline(always)] inside the zero-check table closures; moving it alone proves almost nothing until those closures move
not pure: it replays a transcript (replay_sc) and drags StatementV3, LayerProofV3 and the verifier replay with it
already moved in round 12 (ffn_v3::statement); nothing left to do

pure, and the parked WIP moves them, but they derive the WITNESS and never touch proof bytes directly, so a byte-identity check would be indirect; their natural home (ffn_v3::witness) is the module the out-of-scope V3Witness split needs
pure one-liners; sum_fp2 is currently dead on the v3 path (`let _ = sum_fp2;` at layer.rs 833). Low evidential value for the boundary
pure, but a performance specialization whose correctness argument is about the prover's block layout; splitting it from the prover puts an invariant across a crate boundary for no gain

tests_added.name: eval_many_is_eval_mle_base_on_every_slice
tests_added.what: the moved helper equals mle::eval_mle_base slice by slice over a seeded sample of 0..=12 variables and head/interior/tail offsets; eval_mle_base is an independent oracle already in the core

tests_added.name: eval_many_follows_the_slice_order_and_allows_repeats
tests_added.what: one eq table, several slices: results follow the caller's order, repeats and reversals included, empty list is empty

tests_added.name: the_empty_point_reads_one_element
tests_added.what: the zero-variable case reads a one-element slice as itself

tests_added.name: a_slice_length_that_does_not_match_the_point_panics
tests_added.what: a mismatched slice length is a caller bug, not a silently wrong claim

tests_added.name: eval_many_agrees_with_the_pre_move_implementation
tests_added.what: exact equality against a VERBATIM copy of the pre-move body over a deterministic seeded sample: 0..=12 point variables, 1..=5 slices, head/odd-interior/tail offsets, repeated and reversed slice lists, empty slice list
tests_added.comparisons_derivation: 13 point sizes x (4 + 5 + 4) slices per size; the test itself asserts only the lower bound 100, so 169 is read off the sample definition, not off the run

tests_added.name: v3_layer_proof_bytes_are_unchanged
tests_added.what: sha256 of the whole v3 layer proof on the seeded T2 and T32 (d=f=16, log_cols 5, inv_rate 4, 12 column checks) fixtures equals the pre-move capture, and the proof still verifies
